# Growthbook <> FlowGPT - Sync
Date: 2026-09-09 | Duration: 24.90999984741211m

## Summary
Flow GPT discussed moving from Statsig to GrowthBook’s enterprise plan to reduce costs while maintaining critical experimentation and feature-flagging capabilities. GrowthBook proposed pricing designed to cut costs by half and support a planned 420-seat contract, while Flow GPT currently has 79 active users and may grow to 110–120. Monthly feature-flagging CDN requests are about 33 million. Flow GPT does not plan to migrate full event data, focusing instead on feature-flagging events and exposures, while deeper A/B-test analysis remains internal. The team is investigating an abnormal June-to-July event spike that may result from repeated requests. Experimentation SDKs and feature flagging are top priorities; experiment-progress views are useful but could be built internally. Self-hosting is not favored because reliability and maintenance are critical. Dan will provide multiple contract options, usage details, and migration support, with a decision targeted within a month.

## Keywords
AI-generated content, feature flagging, experimentation, contract negotiation, migration support, event analytics

## Action Items

**Dan Wathne**
Prepare and send two contract proposal options to Alex Xi, one with a lower seat count and one covering full migration seats, including migration support documentation (19:00)
Provide accurate and detailed usage projections and pricing information for Alex Xi to evaluate (21:55)
Be available for live discussions to clarify questions and assist with the migration process as needed (23:10)

**Alex Xi**
Review contract proposals and run internal cost and usage analyses to determine the best option for FlowGPT (21:50)

# Growthbook <> FlowGPT - Pricing Sync
Date: 2026-09-22 | Duration: 14.65999984741211m

## Summary
Dan Wathne proposed discounted Enterprise pricing of about $76,500 for 80 seats, compared with $90,000, including a CDN limit increase, onboarding, private channels, SLAs, SSO, and advanced security. Growth Book currently spends $65,000 on Pro. Alex Xi estimated that 30–40 seats could support engineering-focused feature flagging, while 120 seats might be needed for broader adoption, since many business users mainly visualize experiments and rely on an in-house warehouse and data team for validation. Dan said reducing seats to 40 would save about $12,000 annually because CDN usage drives much of the cost. Read-only seats at $300, half the full-seat price of $600, were proposed for visualization-only users. Dan also offered prorated mid-year seat additions, multiple order-form options for 40 and 100–120 seats, and a waiver of the upcoming approximately $5,500 Pro bill if the Enterprise contract is signed before the next billing cycle.

## Keywords
Enterprise Upgrade, Pricing Discount, Seat Limit, Feature Flags, Case Study, Read-Only Seats

## Action Items

**Dan Wathne**
Provide FlowGPT with an order form including pricing options for both 40 seats and 100-120 seats scenarios to accommodate their organizational needs (13:25)
Include an add-on pricing option for additional read-only seats in the order form as requested by FlowGPT (12:38)
Waive FlowGPT’s upcoming Pro plan bill if they commit to upgrading to the Enterprise plan before the next billing cycle this month to provide cost savings (11:57)

**Alex xi**
Consider the pricing options including the 15% case study discount and provide feedback on moving forward with the Enterprise upgrade (11:51)
Review and decide between the two seat count scenarios (40 seats vs. 100-120 seats) when the order form is provided to optimize cost and coverage (13:49)
